title: AstraZeneca Secures FDA Nod for New Breast Cancer Therapy Etcamah
author: Na
description: The FDA has granted accelerated approval to AstraZeneca's Etcamah (camizestrant) combined with CDK4/6 inhibitors for treating HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. The combination reduced disease progression or death risk by 56% compared to standard treatment. The FDA also approved Guardant360 CDx diagnostic test to identify patients with ESR1 mutations eligible for this therapy.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: FDA approval of Etcamah represents the company's 10th FDA approval this year and 4th in breast cancer, with strong clinical efficacy data showing 56% risk reduction. However, stock has underperformed YTD (-11.5%), and the approval faced initial advisory committee rejection, requiring additional data submission.
Ibrance (palbociclib) is approved as one of three CDK4/6 inhibitors to be used in combination with Etcamah, but this represents a complementary use rather than direct benefit to Pfizer's business.
Kisqali (ribociclib) is approved as one of three CDK4/6 inhibitors to be used in combination with Etcamah, but this represents a complementary use rather than direct benefit to Novartis's business.

Verzenio (abemaciclib) is approved as one of three CDK4/6 inhibitors to be used in combination with Etcamah, but this represents a complementary use rather than direct benefit to Eli Lilly's business.
FDA approval of Guardant360 CDx companion diagnostic test validates the diagnostic tool and strengthens Guardant's multi-year collaboration with AstraZeneca, supporting future revenue opportunities.

title: Global Cancer Biomarkers Market to Reach $37.8 Billion by 2035 as Precision Oncology Adoption Accelerates - Trends and Forecasts Till 2035
author: Researchandmarkets.Com
description: The global cancer biomarkers market is projected to grow from $25.9 billion in 2026 to $37.8 billion by 2035, with a CAGR of 4.3%. Growth is driven by rising cancer incidence, personalized medicine adoption, advances in NGS and liquid biopsy technologies, and increased biomarker-driven diagnostics. HER2 testing leads by biomarker type (21.1% share), while breast cancer testing dominates by indication (25.1% share). North America captures 52.1% of global market revenue.
